Heavy rain, landslides halt Amarnath Yatra in Jammu:Delhi-NCR gridlocked after downpour, 300 homes flooded in Bihar’s Bagaha
The Amarnath Yatra from Jammu was suspended again on Saturday due to heavy rain and landslides in Jammu and Kashmir.
Authorities have warned of heavy rainfall, flooding and landslides across the Jammu region until August 11.
Heavy rain also lashed Delhi on Friday, leaving several major roads, including the Delhi-Gurugram highway, waterlogged.
In some areas, water accumulated to nearly four feet, leaving vehicles stranded and triggering long traffic jams.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for Delhi for Saturday. The national capital has received 127 mm of rainfall in the first week of August, the highest for the period since 2011.
Bihar, UP also affected by heavy rain
In Bihar, heavy rainfall in Nepal has pushed the Bagmati River into spate in Muzaffarpur. In Bagaha, rising water levels in the Gandak River have flooded around 300 houses, prompting authorities to shift residents to safer locations.
Uttar Pradesh has also been affected by prolonged heavy rainfall, with several rivers flowing above normal levels after nearly 25 days of rain.
In Varanasi, rising water levels in the Ganga have submerged several ghats and cut off access to 84 ghats. Water has also entered around 50-60 small temples.
Meanwhile, a road caved in at Agra, creating a nearly 20-foot-deep crater and disrupting movement in the area.

Weather pictures from across the country
Children in Gariaband, Chhattisgarh, crossing waterlogged paths with bags on their heads to go to school.
In Loni area of Ghaziabad, UP, the roads were so waterlogged that children were seen having fun.
Heavy rain occurred in Delhi on Friday. Waterlogging in many areas led to long traffic jams on the roads.
The Kali River is flowing above the danger mark in Dharchula, Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand.
The Bagmati River is in spate in Muzaffarpur, Bihar. Several villages are submerged in up to three feet of water.
